newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila turns down Cent Bank plea for more capital.
newsitem.headline: Manila turns down Cent Bank plea for more capital.

text.p: The Philippine government is not willing to grant the Central Bank's request for an additional 40 billion pesos in capital, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo told reporters on Thursday.

"The 40 billion pesos was intended, in a sense, to bail out a Central Bank that was in bad shape. The Central Bank is not in a bad shape now. And between the Central Bank's needs and the fiscal needs, considering the Central Bank is in a much stronger position now, we must strike a balance," he said.
"I'm not aware yet of the pressing need," he added.
Philippine Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson had urged Congress on Wednesday to pass a resolution to provide the Central Bank with an additional 40 billion pesos in capital.
He said the additional capital was needed to pursue effective monetary and reserve management.

Under the law which created a new Central Bank in 1993, the Central Bank should have capital of 50 billion pesos within a period of two years. Only 10 billion pesos has so far been paid by the national government.

Singson proposed that Congress authorise the government to convert 40 billion pesos of its 50-billion-peso special deposit with the Central Bank into equity, since the deposit cannot be used by the government until 2003.
